title: Python, arrays & vectorized thinking
summary: Learn the programming concepts that connect ordinary code to numerical computing.
html:
Learn the programming concepts that connect ordinary code to numerical computing.

Names, values, and mutation

A Python name refers to an object. Assignment can create another reference rather than another copy. Lists are flexible containers; numerical arrays store elements with a dtype and shape. Mutating an array view can modify the original storage, so understand whether an operation returns a view or a copy.

Shape is part of the contract

A batch of 32 feature vectors with 128 features has shape (32,128). A weight matrix of shape (128,10) maps it to (32,10). Write dimensions next to each intermediate. Broadcasting expands compatible dimensions conceptually; it may avoid copying inputs but still produce a very large output.

Vectorization and the runtime

Calling an array operation delegates loops to compiled numerical code. This reduces Python interpreter overhead and can use SIMD or GPU kernels. It does not make the computational complexity disappear. A vectorized pairwise distance calculation over a million points may still allocate an impossible trillion-entry result.

Build reproducible experiments

Use isolated environments and record dependency versions. Set seeds when comparing runs, but do not assume identical results across hardware or kernels. Keep preprocessing, model code, data versions, and evaluation settings together. Assertions about shapes and finite values catch errors closer to their source.

Worked example

import numpy as np
x = np.array([[1., 2.], [3., 4.]])
w = np.array([[2.], [-1.]])
y = x @ w
assert y.shape == (2, 1)
print(y.ravel())  # [0. 2.]

What goes wrong

Elementwise multiplication (*) and matrix multiplication (@) answer different questions. A computation can run without a shape error and still broadcast along the wrong axis.

Check your understanding

What is the result shape of (8,16) @ (16,4)?

Reveal the explanation

(8,4). The matching inner dimension is summed over; the outer dimensions remain.

How the pieces connect

A usable chapter has a flow of decisions, evidence, and checks. Use this diagram as a navigation aid, then test each step on a small real example.

An operating model for python, arrays & vectorized thinking

Numerical programming is a discipline of contracts. A tensor shape is not decoration: it records which examples, positions, features, heads, or channels an operation is acting on. Most subtle errors occur when an operation is legal under broadcasting but semantically applies an axis in the wrong role.

The diagram is deliberately sequential, but real systems loop. A surprising result may expose a bad representation; a production incident may reveal a missing evaluation slice; a performance limit may require an algorithmic change. The point is to preserve the link between the abstract concept, the evidence you observe, and the decision you make next.

Field guide: four decisions in order

1. Specify shapes

Specify shapes establishes the next constraint. Name every axis and its semantic meaning. Begin by making the object of study explicit. A vague input, target, or operating condition creates ambiguity that later computation cannot repair.

Write down the input boundary and the unit of analysis. This makes it possible to distinguish a missing fact from a mismatch between the question and the data or system.

2. Transform

Transform establishes the next constraint. Use array operations with an explicit dtype. Now make the mechanism inspectable. Prefer a small run whose intermediate values, examples, or traces can be examined before you automate a larger workflow.

Keep a concrete artifact: a small dataset, a notebook cell, a trace, a benchmark command, or a hand-worked calculation. It is the fastest way to surface hidden assumptions.

3. Validate

Validate establishes the next constraint. Assert shape, range, finiteness, and alignment. Treat the first result as a measurement, not a conclusion. Compare it with a baseline and vary one assumption at a time so that the observed change has an interpretable cause.

Check a deliberately awkward case alongside the happy path. Boundary conditions, rare examples, and resource limits reveal more than another aggregate score.

4. Measure

Measure establishes the next constraint. Benchmark representative sizes and allocations. Finish by connecting the result to a real choice. Record the operating range, uncertainty, and the condition under which the next person should stop, escalate, or revisit the earlier steps.

Preserve the decision record with the result. A useful technical chapter leaves enough context for a reader to reproduce the reasoning, challenge it, and choose a safe next action.

When the first approach fails

Do not respond to a weak result by immediately adding scale, complexity, or another framework. First locate the failure: the input may not match the intended problem; the representation may discard a useful signal; the measurement may reward the wrong outcome; or the system may have crossed a memory, latency, reliability, or authority boundary. Change one layer, repeat the smallest useful check, and keep the before-and-after evidence.

Gotcha. A polished output can hide an untested assumption. The most convincing demonstration is a counterexample the workflow handles deliberately, with the limitation stated in the release or research record.

A rigorous way to practice

  1. Specify shapes. Name every axis and its semantic meaning.
  2. Transform. Use array operations with an explicit dtype.
  3. Validate. Assert shape, range, finiteness, and alignment.
  4. Measure. Benchmark representative sizes and allocations.

Keep a tiny hand-calculated input beside every new operation. Print shapes and a few values, then compare the vectorized result to a simple loop before scaling it.

Questions that keep the chapter honest

AskWhy it mattersEvidence to collect
What assumptions does this method make?Every method encodes a view of data, hardware, or behavior.Inputs, representations, constraints, and cases outside the expected range.
What would make the result fail?Failure modes show where an aggregate result is fragile.Boundary cases, counterexamples, slices, and perturbations.
What decision changes if it improves?A metric only matters through an operational action.Baseline, threshold, cost, latency, and human-review consequences.
